text.p: Following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Tallinn City Court passed the death sentence on Romeo Kalda who killed a police officer last April. The defence said they would appeal.
- A Finnish citizen was murdered in Tallinn on December 31. The murderers, a man and a woman, were arrested the next day.
- President Lennart Meri stressed in his year-end speech on December 31 the need for justice, democracy, and a statesmanly attitude, and urged Estonians to be masters of their country.
- Parliament has received a request from the electoral commission in Chechnya to send an observer to January 27 elections.
- A UN-financed poll showed 75 percent of the 20-29 year old Russian residents consider Estonia, not Russia, their country.
- Polls show 21.6 percent of Estonians would prefer Tiit Vahi as prime minister. Andres Tarand came second with 11.9 percent and Edgar Savisaar third with 10.7 percent.
